note: We offer a small menu that changes daily. The chef requests that guests put their whole order in at once.
raw_note: An asterisk (*) marks dishes served raw or under-cooked. Flag the allergy/raw advisory when guests ask.

items.name: Sea Wolf Bakery Baguette
items.desc: les pres sales butter, sea salt
items.story: A baguette from Sea Wolf Bakers in Seattle's Fremont neighborhood, one of the Pacific Northwest's most celebrated naturally leavened bakeries. Baked the same day, served with Belgian-churned les prés salés butter flecked with coarse Camargue sea salt crystals. Simple and non-negotiable — this one never changes.

ingredients.note: Seattle's Fremont neighborhood bakery, founded 2014 by brothers Jesse and Kit Schumann. All breads are naturally leavened using Pacific Northwest grains. Named one of the 100 best bakeries in the U.S. by Food & Wine.

Belgian-churned cultured butter, 82% butterfat, finished with hand-harvested coarse sea salt crystals from the Camargue — a salt marsh region in the south of France. Richer and more complex than standard salted butter.
Flaky finishing salt from Essex, England. Prized for its pyramid-shaped crystals, clean flavor, and satisfying crunch.

items.name: Castelvetrano Olives
items.story: Meaty Nocellara del Belice olives from the Valle del Belice in southwestern Sicily — one of the only olive varieties with a Protected Designation of Origin. Marinated in-house with citrus peel, garlic, chili flake, and olive oil, then finished with a dusting of fennel pollen and rosemary. Bright, buttery, mild.

ingredients.note: Nocellara del Belice variety, named for the Sicilian town of Castelvetrano. PDO-protected, so they can only come from the Valle del Belice. Lye-cured for a clean, buttery flavor with no bitterness — the least aggressive olive on any table.
The fine yellow pollen harvested from wild fennel flowers. Intensely aromatic, floral, and anise-forward — used here as a finishing garnish.

items.allergenNote: Confirmed: the marinade carries garlic (allium) and chili flake. The garlic is marinated in, so it can't be picked out — off limits for an allium allergy. The chili flake also adds a little heat, a heads up for spice-sensitive guests.

items.name: Marcona Almonds
items.desc: rosemary olive oil, fried rosemary, maldon sea salt
items.story: Imported Marcona almonds from Spain's Mediterranean coast, roasted until golden, tossed in rosemary olive oil and Maldon sea salt, then finished with crisp fried rosemary. Rounder and softer than a California almond, with a buttery sweetness that makes them genuinely hard to stop eating.

ingredients.note: A Spanish almond variety grown along the Mediterranean coast — Alicante, Valencia, and Tarragona. Rounder and plumper than California almonds, with a higher oil content and a naturally sweet, buttery flavor. Spain is the primary producer.
Flaky finishing salt from Essex, England — same as on the bread. Tossed on with the rosemary oil after roasting so the crunch stays distinct.

items.name: Farinata
items.desc: chickpea flatbread, house cagliata, seasonal preserve, fresh thyme, sea salt
items.story: A Ligurian chickpea flatbread with roots in 13th-century Genoa — thin, crisp at the edges, soft and nutty in the center. Made in-house from chickpea flour, rosemary olive oil, and water, finished with fresh thyme and sea salt. The housemade cagliatta and a seasonal preserve sit alongside on the plate. Current preserve: rhubarb caramelized onion jam.

ingredients.note: Ancient Ligurian flatbread made from chickpea flour, water, olive oil, and salt — baked in a very hot cast iron pan until the edges are crisp and the center is custardy. Also called cecìna in Tuscany. Naturally gluten-free.

Our housemade fresh cheese — whole milk curdled with lemon juice, then dressed with rosemary-infused olive oil and salt. A fresh, mild, milky curd; closer to a soft ricotta than a mozzarella. Made in-house.
Seasonal preserve made in-house: rhubarb cooked down with caramelized onions, vinegar, and sugar. Tart, sweet, savory — made to work against the richness of the cagliatta.

items.allergenNote: Naturally gluten-free — chickpea flour, no wheat. The cagliatta is plated alongside; for dairy-free it moves to a bowl on the side or comes off entirely, and the preserve stays.

items.name: House Caesar
items.desc: anchovy, parmigiano reggiano, red wine croutons
items.story: Romaine dressed with a classic from-scratch Caesar dressing — champagne vinegar, anchovy, garlic, Parmigiano-Reggiano, egg yolk, Worcestershire, Dijon, black pepper. Topped with boquerones white anchovies and red wine croutons: bread soaked in red wine, butter, garlic, and rosemary, then dehydrated until crisp the whole way through. A clean, honest Caesar.

ingredients.note: White anchovies cured in vinegar rather than salt — mild, tender, and bright. Distinct from the oil-packed brown anchovies in the dressing; these sit on top as a finishing garnish.
Aged Italian hard cheese from the Parma region, with PDO protection. Used both in the dressing (grated) and shaved over the top. Nutty, salty, and complex.
Made in-house: bread soaked in a red wine, butter, garlic, and rosemary mixture, then dehydrated until crisp all the way through. Deeply savory, and the crunch holds up in the dressing.

The dressing is built with egg yolk — emulsified raw with oil and champagne vinegar for a thick, rich, classic Caesar consistency. Not cooked through, similar to mayonnaise. It also carries the anchovy: for fish allergies the dressing has to go, not just the boquerones on top.

items.allergenNote: Every flag has a path, but fish takes two cuts: the dressing itself has anchovy in it, so pulling the boquerones alone doesn't clear it — omit the boquerones AND swap the dressing for oil and vinegar. Croutons on the side handles gluten. The same oil-and-vinegar swap with cheese on the side covers dairy, egg, and allium. Fully modified it becomes a clean romaine salad with oil and vinegar; tell the guest what they're getting.

items.name: Farm House Salad
items.desc: red onion, bread and butter pickled onion, charred apricot vinaigrette, nectarines, candied almonds
items.story: Bright and textured. The charred apricot vinaigrette brings acid and a subtle depth to the greens. Fresh nectarines and candied almonds add sweetness and crunch. Red and pickled onions give you sharp bite throughout.

ingredients.note: Apricots charred on high heat, then blended into a vinaigrette with acid and oil. The char adds a smoky-sweet depth behind the fruit's natural acidity.

A sweet-and-tangy pickle style — onions cured in a vinegar brine with sugar and spice. Despite the name there's no bread or butter; it refers to the classic sweet pickle profile. Bright and sharp against the greens.

Almonds cooked in sugar until glazed and crisp. Adds sweetness and crunch — and the tree-nut allergen on the plate. Confirm the candying method with the kitchen; some preparations also carry butter or egg white.
Smooth-skinned stone fruit, sweeter and softer than a peach when ripe. Fresh and raw here for juicy sweetness.

items.allergenNote: Tree nuts: the candied almonds — they come off cleanly for a nut allergy. Allium: raw red onion and the pickled onion are throughout, not removable. UNCONFIRMED — confirm the candied-almond prep with the kitchen; some candying methods also carry dairy (butter) or egg white. Verify before promising nut-free-adjacent or vegan.

items.name: Burrata
items.desc: strawberries, chamomile gelee, strawberry buttermilk poppy seed vinaigrette, crostini
items.story: Creamy burrata with fresh strawberries and a chamomile gelee that adds subtle floral sweetness. The strawberry buttermilk vinaigrette brings acid and brightness. Crostini on the side for texture.

ingredients.note: a fresh cow's-milk cheese from Puglia: a mozzarella shell holding a center of stracciatella (cheese curds) and cream. Cut into it and the middle should flow.

Chamomile tea set into a soft jelly. Floral, lightly honeyed, and delicate — it echoes the sweetness of the strawberries. Typically set with gelatin, so as plated this is not vegetarian; confirm the setting agent if a guest asks.
A creamy vinaigrette built on cultured buttermilk and strawberry, flecked with poppy seeds. Tangy and bright — the acid that cuts the rich cheese. Carries dairy from the buttermilk.

items.allergenNote: Dairy: the burrata and the buttermilk vinaigrette — central, not removable. Gluten: crostini come on the side so the rest of the table can still have them. UNCONFIRMED: the vinaigrette has poppy seeds (an allergen in some regions, not one we track as a chip) and the chamomile gelee is likely gelatin-set, so as plated this is not vegetarian — verify both with the kitchen before promising.

items.name: Chilled Cherry Gazpacho
items.desc: bing cherry, tomato, cucumber, red onion, bell pepper, champagne vinegar, crème fraiche, sumac
items.story: Cold soup built on bing cherries and tomatoes with cucumber, red onion, and red bell pepper. Champagne vinegar adds brightness. Finished with crème fraiche and sumac for tang and color.

ingredients.note: A cold, raw-blended Spanish soup of vegetables and acid, served chilled. This version leans on bing cherries alongside the tomato for a sweet-savory depth.
Dark, sweet summer cherry — deep red, rich, and low in acidity. Here it carries the soup's body and sweetness against the tomato and vinegar.
French cultured cream — thicker and tangier than sour cream, milder than Greek yogurt. Swirled in to finish, for richness and a cool counterpoint to the acid.
A tart, deep-red Middle Eastern spice ground from dried sumac berries. Lemony and astringent — dusted on top for color and a bright, sour lift.

items.allergenNote: Naturally gluten-free. Dairy: the crème fraiche finish can come off cleanly. Allium: red onion and garlic are blended into the base — not removable.

items.name: Swan House Bolognese
items.desc: saffron spaghetti, swan house beef & pork, tomato, fennel, rosemary, parmigiano reggiano
items.story: The family recipe — on the menu since day one, and it never leaves. This run is built on ground beef and pork raised at Swan House Farm; when it's gone, the dish returns to the classic pork-and-veal build. Either way: seasoned with our own spice blend, cooked down slowly with red wine, tomato, fennel, and rosemary, then finished with cream, butter, sherry, and salt. The saffron spaghetti is extruded with a strained, highly concentrated saffron tea in place of water — that's where the gold color and the subtle earthy aroma come from, no egg involved.

ingredients.note: a slow-cooked meat ragù from Bologna in Emilia-Romagna — traditionally more meat than tomato.

the dried stigma of the crocus flower, hand-harvested and prized. We brew it into a concentrated tea, strain it, and use it in place of water in the extruded dough — gold color, hay-like earthiness, and the reason this golden pasta has no egg.
the aged hard cheese from Emilia-Romagna, the only 'real' Parmesan; nutty, savory, crystalline.

items.allergenNote: No egg in the saffron spaghetti. Dairy: the kitchen can finish it without cream, butter, or Parmigiano — a leaner, brighter ragù. Built in and non-negotiable: allium, the cooked red wine, chili flake, and black pepper.

items.name: Rigatoni
items.desc: roasted broccoli, onion, bread-crumble cream, garlic, shallot, chili flake, lemon, pecorino romano, pine nuts
items.story: Broccoli and onion roasted until caramelized, then built into a pan sauce with garlic, shallot, red chili flake, and cubed bread. White wine and cream go in, and the bread melts down as it cooks to thicken it. Finished with lemon juice, zest, and butter, then topped with Pecorino Romano and pine nuts.

ingredients.note: Ridged tube pasta, shorter and narrower than paccheri. The ridges and hollow centers grab and hold the sauce.

The sauce thickener — cubed bread cooked into the roasted broccoli, onion, garlic, shallot, and chili with white wine and cream until the bread melts down and bodies the sauce. Carries gluten (bread) and dairy (cream).
A hard, salty sheep's-milk cheese from Lazio — sharper than Parmigiano. Grated over the finish.
Soft, buttery seeds of the stone pine, toasted for the finish. Treated as a tree-nut allergen on the plate.

items.allergenNote: Gluten and dairy are both built into the sauce — the cubed bread melts in to thicken it, and the cream, butter, and Pecorino carry the dairy, so neither comes out cleanly. Allium: onion, garlic, and shallot are all roasted or cooked into the sauce, not removable. Tree nuts: pine nuts finish the plate, and per the kitchen notes they may also go into the pan — do NOT clear this for a nut allergy until Chris confirms they can be left out entirely.

items.name: Beef Ragù
items.desc: fresh egg pappardelle, ground beef, tomato, garlic, onion, basil, parmigiano reggiano
items.story: Ground beef cooked down low and slow with tomato, garlic, onion, and basil until it's soft and rich. Tossed with fresh egg pappardelle and finished with Parmigiano Reggiano and a little more basil.

ingredients.note: A slow-cooked Italian meat sauce — here ground beef braised down with tomato, garlic, onion, and basil until soft and rich. Built around the meat, with just enough tomato to bind it.
Wide, flat egg-pasta ribbons, broader than tagliatelle. A fresh egg dough, so it carries egg and wheat; the wide surface holds a hearty ragù well.
The aged hard cheese from Emilia-Romagna, the only 'real' Parmesan; nutty, savory, crystalline. Grated over the finish.

items.allergenNote: Egg and gluten are both in the fresh egg pappardelle — no way around them. Dairy: the Parmigiano finish can come off for a leaner plate. Allium: garlic and onion are cooked down into the ragù base, not removable.

items.name: Mafaldine alla Carbonara
items.desc: guanciale, black pepper, swan house farm egg yolk, pecorino romano
items.story: The Roman classic on mafaldine — wide, ruffled ribbon pasta named after Princess Mafalda of Savoy — whose wavy edges catch and hold the glossy sauce. Rendered guanciale, lots of cracked black pepper, Pecorino Romano, and a Swan House Farm egg yolk emulsified into a peppery, silky coating. No cream — the silk comes from the egg and cheese. Served with a raw yolk, hence the asterisk.

ingredients.note: Wide, flat pasta with ruffled edges on both sides, from Naples. Named in honor of Princess Mafalda of Savoy — also called reginette (little queens). The wavy edges grip the carbonara sauce exceptionally well.
a Roman sauce of egg, hard cheese, cured pork, and black pepper — emulsified, never creamed.
cured pork jowl, fattier and more delicate than pancetta; renders down into the sauce.
a hard, salty sheep's-milk cheese from Lazio — sharper than Parmigiano.

items.allergenNote: All the mods exist, none are recommended. Guanciale can come off for vegetarian — the kitchen subs in whatever vegetable is running seasonally on the menu. Dairy or even the egg can technically be left out, at which point it's pasta and pepper; we get the no-egg request more than we'd like, so set expectations honestly. No allium in the dish.

items.name: Risotto alle Zucchine
items.desc: roasted zucchini, parmesan, crème fraîche-basil puree, lemon
items.story: Creamy risotto built on roasted zucchini, garlic, and shallot. Finished with butter, Parmesan, and a basil puree blended from basil, zucchini, crème fraîche, and lemon oil. Bright, clean, and seasonal.

ingredients.note: Italian for 'risotto with zucchini.' A summer take on the dish — roasted zucchini folded through the rice, finished bright with lemon and basil.

Basil, zucchini, crème fraîche, and lemon oil blended smooth into a vivid green puree. Herbaceous and bright with a little richness from the crème fraîche — swirled in at the finish, with micro basil on top for aroma. Note the crème fraîche: this puree carries dairy.
Short-grain Italian rice that releases starch as it cooks, creating risotto's signature creamy texture. Par-cooked in batches at the restaurant, finished per plate to order.

items.allergenNote: Naturally gluten-free. Dairy lives in three spots: Parmesan, butter, and the crème fraîche in the basil puree — a true dairy-free plate means dropping all three, including the puree, so flag it to the kitchen. Allium and the cooked wine can't come out — our risotto base is always par-cooked with onion and white wine in the stock, and this build adds garlic and shallot.

items.name: Pan Roasted Halibut
items.desc: green pea hummus, grilled asparagus, sea bean, shallot, parsley, lemon
items.story: Halibut seared in the pan until the skin crisps. Green pea hummus anchors the plate with mild earthiness. Grilled asparagus and sea beans bring char and brine. Shallot and parsley sharpen it all up, lemon juice and olive oil finish clean.

ingredients.note: Pacific halibut from WA and AK landings. Large flatfish with firm, mild, white flesh. Season runs March through November — spring and summer fish are leaner and more delicate.

A blended spread of green peas in the style of chickpea hummus — bright, mild, and earthy. IMPORTANT: traditional hummus is built with tahini (sesame paste); confirm with the kitchen whether this version uses tahini before serving any guest with a sesame allergy.
A crisp, salty succulent that grows in coastal salt marshes and tidal flats. Also called samphire or pickleweed. Naturally briny — adds a saline crunch against the fish.
Fresh parsley finishes the plate green and herbaceous. Bright, clean, and grassy against the rich fish.

items.allergenNote: Fish: halibut, central. Allium: shallot — comes off cleanly. UNCONFIRMED — SESAME: the green pea hummus is likely built with tahini (sesame paste), which is how hummus is traditionally made. This is NOT yet confirmed for this prep. Do not clear this dish for a sesame-allergic guest until Chris confirms whether the hummus contains tahini.

items.name: Pure Country Pork Chop
items.desc: polenta, charred spring onion, apricot mostarda, demi glace
items.story: Thick cut pork chop served over creamy polenta with charred spring onions for a little smoke and sharpness. Apricot mostarda brings a sweet-tart punch, and demi glace ties it all together. A straightforward dish that lets the pork and its sides speak.

ingredients.note: A Northern Italian condiment made from fruit — here apricot — preserved in a sweet, mustard-oil-spiked syrup. Simultaneously sweet, sharp, fruity, and savory. Traditionally served with rich meats to cut through fat. Despite the name, it is built with mustard essence — flag it for a mustard allergy.

A rich, glossy reduction of meat stock and wine, cooked down until concentrated and silky. Built on a base of onions and aromatics, so it carries cooked allium. Deep and savory — the sauce that pulls the plate together.
Young onions charred on high heat — sweet, smoky, and a little sharp. A direct allium element on the plate, alongside the spring onion's mild bite.
Ground cornmeal cooked with cream, chicken stock, and butter until thick and creamy. Serves as the bed for the chop — rich, mild, and soft.

items.allergenNote: Dairy: the polenta comes off or swaps to a dairy-free starch. Allium: the demi glace is built on onions and the charred spring onions sit on top — the kitchen can sub out the spring onions and the demi entirely, or the guest can keep the demi if cooked-in allium works. UNCONFIRMED — MUSTARD: apricot mostarda is made with mustard essence/oil; we don't track mustard as a chip, but flag it for any mustard-allergic guest and confirm with the kitchen.

food.intro: The egg rule for our pastas, before you get asked: every pasta is made in-house, and the dough tells you everything. Extruded shapes — pushed through a die — are semolina and water, no egg. Hand-made shapes — rolled ribbons like tagliatelle, filled agnolotti, gnocchi — are egg doughs. Rule of thumb: if the shape doesn't seem possible to roll by hand (creste di gallo, bucatini, spaghetti), it's probably extruded. But some shapes that are usually hand-rolled, like linguine or chitarra, can be extruded too — confirm with the chef before assuming. Color helps: egg pasta runs golden and silky, extruded runs pale straw. One trap, though — the bolognese's saffron spaghetti is golden from saffron tea, not egg.

desserts.name: Earl Grey Tiramisu
desserts.desc: mascarpone, ladyfingers, miro tea, planteray dark rum, bergamot agrumato
desserts.story: A San Fermo riff on the Italian classic. Instead of espresso, the ladyfingers are soaked in Earl Grey from Miro Tea — Ballard's 200-variety loose leaf tea shop — which swaps coffee's bitterness for bergamot's floral citrus. Planteray dark rum in the mascarpone cream; bergamot agrumato oil at the finish.

ingredients.note: Classic Northern Italian dessert — ladyfinger biscuits soaked in liquid, layered with sweetened mascarpone cream, finished with cocoa. The name means "pick me up" in Italian.
Ballard neighborhood tea shop, Seattle, founded 2005. Carries over 200 varieties of loose leaf tea. We use their Earl Grey for the ladyfinger soak — clean, bergamot-forward, and bright.

Extra virgin olive oil co-milled with whole bergamot fruit at the press — the citrus oils are captured inside the olive oil rather than infused afterward. Bergamot is the citrus that gives Earl Grey its distinctive floral-bitter aroma. Used as a finishing drizzle here.

Formerly Plantation Rum — rebranded to Planteray in 2024. French-Caribbean aged rum from Maison Ferrand, known for its dual aging: first in the tropics, then finished in cognac barrels in France. Rich, smooth, and molasses-forward.
Italian triple-cream fresh cheese from Lombardy — thick, rich, mildly sweet. The base of the tiramisu cream layer.

desserts.name: Pavlova
desserts.desc: rose meringue, vanilla pastry cream, macerated strawberries
desserts.story: A crisp-outside, marshmallow-inside meringue, named for the Russian ballerina Anna Pavlova. This one's rose-scented, topped with a cloud of vanilla pastry cream and fresh macerated strawberries. Light, a little floral, and sweet without being heavy.

ingredients.note: a meringue-based dessert with a crisp crust and soft center, named for ballerina Anna Pavlova.
whipped egg whites and sugar, baked low and slow until crisp.
fruit softened and drawn out with a little sugar until juicy and glossy.

desserts.allergenNote: No flour in the meringue — gluten-free as built. The pastry cream rides on the side for dairy-free; the meringue and strawberries stand on their own.

desserts.name: Seasonal Gelato
desserts.desc: ask the kitchen for tonight's flavor
desserts.allergenNote: Flavors rotate nightly — confirm eggs or nuts with the kitchen before promising anything.
